subject: ventures/construction-evidence-log
professional: a construction project manager / construction claims consultant who assembles daily-report and change-order records for payment and delay disputes; first checks: does a day's record carry the fields a contemporaneous daily report needs (manpower by trade and hours, equipment, deliveries, inspections/visitors, safety, instructions received, time of entry), can the record show it was not rewritten later, does a change entry capture who directed it, in what form, its cost/time and whether written approval or notice is outstanding, and do the multi-day pack counts reconcile.

evidence.correctness: Drove the real page in headless Chrome (served copy of the directory plus a driver script, /tmp/claude-0/audit-construction-evidence-log/site/driver.js): four submissions, project filter, combined pack, CSV and single-day download. Independent recomputation: the exported CSV parsed with Python's csv module (RFC 4180 reader the author did not write) gives 5 rows x 11 columns with embedded commas, doubled quotes and a newline in 'work' recovered exactly; pack entries are date-sorted and dateRange 2026-08-25..2026-08-27 matches Python sorted(); the default date equals the local date from Intl.DateTimeFormat in America/Los_Angeles, Pacific/Auckland and UTC. Fails: packSummary says '4 days logged (2026-08-25 to 2026-08-27)' and '1 of 4 days include a change or delay' for 3 distinct dates, because a resubmitted (corrected) day is a second entry and entryCount is labelled as days (record.mjs:111,113); the CSV writes '=HYPERLINK("http://x","y")' unneutralised, contrary to OWASP CSV-injection guidance, so a cell typed by anyone on site becomes a live formula in the spreadsheet the pack is handed to. The tie-break comparator never returns 0, so two entries with equal date and savedAt order by input order.
evidence.completeness: Every feature the README and page list worked end to end in the browser run: form -> record + review notes ('People on site was left blank' for blank crew), local save (storedCount 4), history list with notes badge, per-project filter, combined JSON pack (named construction-evidence-pack-oak-st-2026-08-25_to_2026-08-27.json), CSV (construction-evidence-log-oak-st.csv), single-day JSON, copy summary path, delete/clear-all wired (ids checked by page.test.mjs). No stubs or TODOs. Links to the change-order article, vs-procore page and sibling calculator exist. Gaps: no way to edit or supersede an entry (resubmitting creates a duplicate), no import of a downloaded pack back into another browser.
evidence.verification: `node --test '*.test.mjs'`: 27 pass in 0.08 s. quality_mutate.py: 5 seeded mutants, 4 survived: reversing the savedAt tie-break (record.mjs:51), excluding type 'both' from the change/delay count (record.mjs:58), turning the exact project filter into a substring match (app.js:85), and dropping the missing-requester note for delays (record.mjs:25). Only reversing the primary date sort (record.mjs:50) was caught. app.js has no behavioural test at all (page.test.mjs only checks that ids exist and strings appear), and no test covers 'both', duplicate same-day entries or CSV formula cells.
evidence.craft: Read record.mjs (118 lines), app.js (252), index.html, page.test.mjs, record.test.mjs, vs-procore.test.mjs. Small, pure core module, escaped innerHTML (an work entry rendered as text, no element injected), storage wrapped in try/catch, DNT/GPC honoured. Defects: the three download handlers repeat the Blob/anchor/revoke block (app.js:185-239); escHtml is a minified one-liner unlike the rest; sort comparator is not a consistent comparator (never 0); entryCount reused as a day count; makeRecord does not flag a blank 'work' or an unknown changeType (relies on the form's required attribute and select).
evidence.claims: Checked: disclaimer and 'not legal... engineering advice' on index, README and vs-procore (pass); 'Everything runs in your browser... nothing uploaded' (pass: no fetch/XHR in app.js, no third-party script); local-storage persistence and delete/clear copy matches app.js (pass); Procore 'founded 2002, headquartered in Carpinteria, California' and no Procore price stated (pass, consistent with Procore's public filings); non-affiliation statement (pass). Fails: the change-order article still says 'Keep your own backup... the tool holds nothing for you' (how-do-i-document-a-change-order.html:52) though every entry is now saved in the browser; README's list of counted events omits csv_downloaded (app.js:212); the filter note says project 'matches exactly' but the match is case- and whitespace-insensitive, and the pack then lists 'Oak St, oak st' as two projects; the pack summary's 'N days logged' overcounts; llms.txt:5 carries calculator boilerplate ('Results are estimates from the numbers typed in') for a log tool. Live page returned a proxy 403; served-copy.mjs reports no placeholder or retired origin in what ships.
evidence.fitness: A small sub could keep a same-day text log of crew, conditions, work and a change/delay note and hand over a dated JSON or CSV, which beats a text thread. A PM or claims consultant would hit within the first hour: records live in one browser on one device with no sync or re-import; a corrected day cannot be edited, only duplicated, and the duplicate is counted as another day; no photos, hours, equipment, deliveries or inspections; no signature or acknowledgement; a JSON file anyone can edit with no hash or chain to show it was not altered after the dispute arose. Usable for informal record keeping, not as the record a dispute rests on.
evidence.domain: Compared against the contractor daily report fields in USACE/UFGS 01 45 00 (Contractor Quality Control daily report: weather, manpower by trade and hours, equipment, work performed by location, tests/inspections, deliveries, safety, instructions received, signature) and AIA A201-2017 Article 7 (changes by signed Change Order or Construction Change Directive) and 15.1.3 (claims notice within 21 days). The tool captures weather/conditions, a free-text crew field, work, and a change with requester, free-text impact and details. It departs on: hours and trade breakdown, equipment, deliveries, inspections, safety, time of the direction, form of the direction (verbal/text/drawing, which its own article lists as essential), written-approval or notice status and dates, cost as a number, and integrity (hash or append-only history). The review notes check field presence only. Stated limits ('evidence-only', does not determine entitlement) are honest but the method is a notes form, not a daily report a PM would sign off.

mutations.change: const changeCount = sorted.filter((e) => e.record.change).length; -> const changeCount = sorted.filter((e) => e.record.change && e.record.change.type !== 'both').length;
if (da !== db) return da < db ? -1 : 1; -> if (da !== db) return da > db ? -1 : 1;

defects.what: packSummary labels entryCount as days: a corrected day (resubmitted, since entries cannot be edited) is counted as another day, so 4 entries over 3 dates read '4 days logged' and '1 of 4 days include a change or delay' in the summary handed to a PM.
CSV export does not neutralise cells starting with = + - @ (OWASP CSV injection); text typed on site such as '=HYPERLINK(...)' becomes a live formula when the CSV is opened by the recipient.

Tests miss core changes: 4 of 5 seeded mutants survive (tie-break order, change/delay count for type 'both', project filter semantics, missing-requester note for delays); app.js has no behavioural test.

Daily report scope departs from contractor daily-report practice (UFGS 01 45 00 CQC report; AIA A201 Art. 7 / 15.1.3): no hours or trade breakdown, equipment, deliveries, inspections, safety, time and form of the direction, written-approval or notice status, numeric cost; no integrity hash or append-only history, and no edit/supersede, so a correction is an unlinked duplicate.
Change-order article says 'the tool holds nothing for you', contradicting the local-storage history the tool now keeps.
README's list of counted events omits csv_downloaded, which app.js records.
History note says the project 'matches exactly' but the filter is case- and whitespace-insensitive, and the pack then lists 'Oak St' and 'oak st' as two projects.
llms.txt carries calculator boilerplate ('Results are estimates from the numbers typed in') for a record-keeping tool.
Three download handlers duplicate the Blob/anchor/revoke block; sort comparator never returns 0.

verdict: A small, honest, browser-local daily log that does everything it lists: driven in headless Chrome, it saved four entries, filtered by project, and produced a date-sorted combined JSON pack, a CSV that Python's RFC 4180 reader parses exactly, and a single-day file, with escaped history and an accurate privacy and no-warranty notice. It misses the bar on correctness, verification and claims: the pack summary counts entries as days (a corrected day becomes '4 days logged' for 3 dates), the CSV passes formula cells through unneutralised, 4 of 5 seeded mutants survive the 27 tests, and the change-order article still says the tool stores nothing. A construction PM or claims consultant would also find it a notes form rather than a daily report: no hours, equipment, deliveries, inspections, safety, approval/notice status or integrity hash. Finished as scoped; not a record a dispute could rest on.
